Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and re-approved each year after the NAIC issues the new-year Statement Instructions and AP&P Manual updates; interim re-approval on any adopted SSAP revision that changes a blank line

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Blank must be complete and Jurat-signed at least 5 business days before the 45-day statutory due date — May 15 (Q1), August 14 (Q2), November 14 (Q3) — and 10 business days before March 1 for the Annual Blank

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar tasks fire at quarter-end +10 (TB frozen), +20 (SAP adjustments booked), +30 (all pages drafted, cross-checks run), +38 (Jurat signed) for every quarter-end

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed blank PDF, TB-to-blank mapping workbook, SAP adjustment journal support, cross-check clearance report and the actuarial reserve handoff retained 7 years from the filing date in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any post-Jurat restatement, unresolved cross-check override, or blank line unsupported by the TB mapping is logged as a statutory reporting exception with root cause, the amended-blank decision and a remediation date

checklist.step: Lock the quarterly close calendar and freeze the statutory trial balance
actions: Publish the close calendar to Finance, Actuarial, Investment Operations and Reinsurance Accounting with the quarter-end +10 TB freeze date backed off the 45-day due date (May 15 for Q1, August 14 for Q2, November 14 for Q3).
In the general ledger open Financial Close ▸ Period Status and set the reporting period to Closed for each writing company's statutory ledger once the last subledger has posted.
Export the frozen trial balance by legal entity and account, and record the export timestamp, row count and total debits/credits on the close control sheet.
Confirm with the Reinsurance Accountant and the Investment Operations Manager in writing that their subledgers have been posted and no late entries are pending.
File the frozen TB export in the financial reporting repository as the single source for the blank.
checklist.done: the period is closed in the GL for every writing company and a timestamped frozen TB export is filed with debits equal to credits.

checklist.step: Map every trial balance account to its NAIC blank line
actions: Open the statutory reporting software, select the current-year Quarterly Blank for the company type (P&C, Life/Fraternal or Health) and import the frozen TB.
Work the account mapping table so every TB account carries a blank line reference — Page 2 asset lines, Page 3 liability and surplus lines, Page 4 income lines.
Run the unmapped-account report and clear it to zero; any new GL account opened in the quarter must be mapped before it reaches the blank.
Get the Senior Accountant who owns each GL account group to initial the mapping for their accounts.
Save the mapping workbook with the quarter stamp beside the frozen TB in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the unmapped-account report is empty and every mapped account group carries a preparer initial and a blank line reference.

checklist.step: Identify and book the statutory-only (SAP) adjustments off the GAAP-basis ledger
actions: Work the standing SAP adjustment inventory: nonadmit furniture, EDP equipment over the SSAP No. 16 limit, prepaid expenses and receivables over 90 days past due; reverse GAAP DAC; restate deferred tax to the SSAP No. 101 admissibility test.
Pull the aged premium receivable report from the billing platform and compute the over-90-day balance to be nonadmitted, agreeing the cut-off date to quarter end.
Post each adjustment as a separate statutory-ledger journal with the SSAP reference in the description and the supporting schedule attached.
Hand the deferred tax admissibility computation to the Tax Manager for confirmation and file the reply.
Reconcile GAAP surplus to statutory capital and surplus on a bridge schedule listing every adjustment and its amount.
checklist.done: the GAAP-to-SAP surplus bridge foots to statutory capital and surplus and every adjustment cites a SSAP and has attached support.

checklist.step: Build Assets (Page 2) with the nonadmitted column
actions: In the statutory reporting software open the Assets page and let the mapping populate Column 1 (Assets), then enter Column 2 (Nonadmitted Assets) from the nonadmitted schedule so Column 3 (Net Admitted) computes.
Agree bonds, common stocks, mortgage loans, real estate and cash/short-term lines to the investment accounting extract supplied by Investment Operations, line by line.
Agree uncollected premiums and agents' balances to the billing platform aged report, split into deferred and not-yet-due versus over 90 days.
Check Page 2 Line 28 total net admitted assets ties to the prior-quarter blank plus the movement on the surplus bridge.
Note in the workbook any line moving more than 10% from the prior quarter with the driver, ready for the analyst question.
checklist.done: Page 2 net admitted assets agrees to the investment and receivable subledgers and every line moving over 10% has a written driver.

checklist.step: Build Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds (Page 3)
actions: Enter losses, loss adjustment expenses and unearned premium from the reserve handoff and the policy administration unearned premium register.
Enter ceded reinsurance premiums payable, funds held and provision for reinsurance from the ceded accounting balances confirmed by the Reinsurance Accountant.

Roll the capital and surplus section: prior-quarter surplus, net income, change in nonadmitted assets, change in net deferred income tax, change in provision for reinsurance, dividends to stockholders.
Prove Page 3 total liabilities plus capital and surplus equals Page 2 Line 28 net admitted assets to the dollar.
Have the Controller initial the surplus roll-forward before it is treated as final.
checklist.done: Page 3 balances to Page 2 to the dollar and the surplus roll-forward is initialled by the Controller.

checklist.step: Build the Statement of Income (Page 4) and the Capital and Surplus Account
actions: Populate premiums earned, losses incurred, LAE incurred, other underwriting expenses, net investment income earned and net realized capital gains from the mapped TB.
Agree net investment income earned and realized gains/losses to the investment accounting income report for the year-to-date period, not the quarter alone — the blank is year-to-date.
Enter the federal and foreign income tax provision agreed with the Tax Manager, and reconcile it to the tax provision memo.
Check the year-to-date columns roll from the prior-quarter blank plus the current quarter's movement, and that prior-year comparatives agree to the filed Annual Blank.
Document any reclassification between underwriting and investment income with the rationale.
checklist.done: Page 4 year-to-date figures roll from the prior-quarter blank and comparatives agree to the filed Annual Blank.

checklist.step: Build the Cash Flow statement (Page 5)
actions: Populate Cash from Operations (premiums collected net of reinsurance, net investment income, benefit and loss payments, commissions and expenses paid, federal income taxes paid).
Populate Cash from Investments from the investment accounting proceeds and cost-of-acquired report, and Cash from Financing and Miscellaneous Sources.
Prove the net change in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments ties to the movement in the Page 2 cash lines between the prior year-end and this quarter end.
Ask the Treasury Analyst to confirm the bank-side cash movement for the period and reconcile any difference before signing the page off.
Attach the cash flow support workbook to the close file.
checklist.done: the Page 5 net change in cash ties to the Page 2 cash line movement and is confirmed against Treasury's bank movement.

checklist.step: Take the reserve handoff from Actuarial and load the reserve lines
actions: Run the quarterly reserve review in the reserving platform on data evaluated at quarter end and produce the booked indication by line of business, gross and net of reinsurance.
Issue a signed reserve handoff memo to the Controller stating the booked case and IBNR figures for loss and for LAE, the evaluation date and the data cut used.
Reconcile the paid and case reserve data underlying the review to the claims platform ledger extract and note any difference over 1%.
Where the booked figure differs from the actuarial central estimate, state the amount and the reason in the memo.
File the memo and the supporting exhibits in the financial reporting repository against the quarter.
checklist.done: a signed reserve handoff memo with gross and net loss and LAE figures is filed and reconciles to the claims data extract.

checklist.step: Bring in ceded reinsurance balances and the quarterly Schedule F content
actions: Extract ceded balances by reinsurer from the ceded accounting platform: paid and unpaid recoverables, ceded unearned premium, funds held and collateral (letters of credit, trust balances).
Match each reinsurer to its NAIC company code and confirm authorized / unauthorized / certified status for the domiciliary state as at quarter end.
Compute the provision for reinsurance on unauthorized and overdue balances and hand the figure to the Statutory Reporting Manager for the Page 3 line.
Chase any recoverable over 90 days overdue with the Reinsurance Manager and record the collection status.
File the reinsurer-level schedule as support for the blank's reinsurance lines.
checklist.done: ceded balances are extracted by reinsurer with authorized status and the provision for reinsurance figure is delivered with support.

checklist.step: Complete the quarterly Notes to Financial Statements
actions: Work the quarterly Notes set required by the NAIC Quarterly Statement Instructions — accounting changes and corrections of errors, fair value, investments, reinsurance, income taxes, related party transactions, subsequent events, and reserve development.
Update the one-year reserve development disclosure from the reserve handoff memo and agree the figure to the roll-forward.
Ask Legal Counsel for the contingent liabilities and litigation update and paste the cleared wording into the Notes.
Carry forward the prior Notes and mark every changed paragraph so the reviewer sees the delta rather than re-reading the whole set.
Remove any Note that is annual-only so the quarterly Notes set matches the instructions exactly.
checklist.done: the quarterly Notes set matches the instruction list, carries an updated development disclosure and a cleared litigation paragraph.

checklist.step: Answer the General Interrogatories and the supplemental interrogatories
actions: Open General Interrogatories Part 1 (General) and Part 2 (line-of-business specific) in the blank and answer every question — no blanks, no 'N/A' where a number is required.
Confirm ownership, holding company and change-of-control answers with the Corporate Secretary against the current Schedule Y organisational chart.
Confirm custodial and safekeeping agreement answers with the Investment Operations Manager, naming each custodian.
Compare each answer to the prior quarter and write the reason for every change on the interrogatory support sheet.
Route the completed interrogatories to Legal Counsel for the questions on litigation, regulatory action and officer bonding.
checklist.done: every interrogatory is answered, changes from the prior quarter are explained, and legal and custodial answers are confirmed by their owners.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC cross-check and validation edits and clear every hit
actions: In the statutory reporting software run the full validation suite: NAIC cross-checks, prior-period comparisons, blank-to-blank ties and the electronic filing edits.
Work the error report to zero errors; treat every 'error' as blocking and every 'warning' as requiring a written explanation.
For each warning left in place, enter the explanation text that will accompany the electronic filing, naming the amount and the reason.
Re-run the suite after any correction so the final run is clean, and export the final validation report as evidence.
Escalate to the Controller any edit that cannot be cleared without a restatement of a prior filed period.
checklist.done: the final validation run shows zero errors, every retained warning has an explanation, and the report is exported to the close file.

checklist.step: Complete the Jurat page and obtain officer attestation
actions: Check the Jurat page carries the correct NAIC company code, FEIN, state of domicile, statutory home office and main administrative office addresses, and the current officer and director listing.
Confirm the director list against the latest board minutes supplied by the Corporate Secretary and correct any resignation or appointment since the last filing.
Read the blank as a whole against the surplus bridge and the reserve handoff memo before signing.
Sign the Jurat with the two additional officers required by the instructions, and have it notarised where the domiciliary state still requires notarisation.
Release the signed blank to Regulatory Reporting for filing no later than 5 business days before the 45-day due date.
checklist.done: a signed Jurat with correct company identifiers and a board-agreed officer/director list is released to Regulatory Reporting ahead of the internal cut-off.

checklist.step: Perform the independent second review of the completed blank
actions: Review the analytical pack: quarter-over-quarter and prior-year-same-quarter movement on every Page 2-5 line with an explanation for each variance over 10% or $1m, whichever is lower.
Re-check the three hard ties — Page 2 to Page 3, Page 4 to the surplus roll-forward, Page 5 to the cash line movement.
Confirm each page carries a named preparer and a different named reviewer on the sign-off grid.
Return anything unexplained to the preparer with a same-day deadline rather than filing with an open question.
Sign the close control sheet to release the blank.
checklist.done: the analytical pack explains every material movement, all three ties hold, and the close control sheet is signed with preparer and reviewer named per page.

checklist.step: Archive the blank and its full support for the retention period
actions: File in the financial reporting repository under company / year / quarter: signed blank PDF, frozen TB export, mapping workbook, SAP adjustment support, GAAP-to-SAP surplus bridge, reserve handoff memo, ceded schedule and the final validation report.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the filing date so the record survives a full financial examination cycle.
Confirm the index makes the record searchable by NAIC company code, statement year and quarter.
Send the Controller the archive link as the close-out of the quarter.
checklist.done: the complete support set is archived under a 7-year label and retrievable by NAIC company code, year and quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of blank lines and tie it to the frozen trial balance
actions: Export from the statutory reporting software every populated line on Pages 2, 3, 4 and 5 plus the quarterly schedules, for every writing company, with the line number and amount.
Export the frozen TB and the SAP adjustment journal listing independently from the general ledger rather than taking Finance's copy.
Rebuild total net admitted assets and capital and surplus from TB plus adjustments and compare to the blank; investigate any difference before sampling.
Record the population line count, the company list and the extract timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the rebuilt net admitted assets and surplus agree to the blank, and the population line count and extract timestamps are recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the account mapping and prove no account escaped the blank
actions: Join the TB account list to the mapping table and list every account with no blank line reference.
List every account opened in the general ledger during the quarter and confirm each one appears in the mapping table.
Sum the mapped amounts by blank line and compare to the blank line amounts; differences over $1,000 per line are exceptions.
Treat any unmapped account with a non-zero balance as an automatic exception regardless of size.
testing.done: every TB account with a balance is mapped and the mapped sums agree to the blank line amounts within $1,000.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of blank lines and SAP adjustments
actions: Take 100% of lines above 1% of capital and surplus, all reserve and reinsurance lines, and all lines that moved more than 25% from the prior quarter.
Draw 20 further lines at random from the remainder using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Take 100% of SAP adjustments over $250,000 and 10 at random below that.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and coverage percentage in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers every line above 1% of surplus and all reserve and reinsurance lines.

testing.step: Re-perform the nonadmitted asset computation on the sample
actions: Pull the aged premium receivable report as at quarter end directly from the billing platform and recompute the over-90-days-past-due balance to be nonadmitted.
Recompute the nonadmitted amounts for furniture, EDP equipment and prepaid expenses and check each cites the SSAP relied on.
Re-perform the SSAP No. 101 deferred tax admissibility test and compare to the booked admitted deferred tax asset.
Any difference between the recomputed and booked nonadmitted total is an exception with the dollar amount stated.
testing.done: recomputed nonadmitted assets agree to the Page 2 Column 2 total, or each difference is quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Trace the reserve lines to the actuarial handoff and the claims system
actions: Agree the Page 3 loss and LAE reserve lines, gross and net, to the signed reserve handoff memo figure by line of business.
Agree the case reserve and paid loss data feeding the reserving platform to a claims platform extract at the same evaluation date.
Confirm the memo is dated before the Jurat signature date — a reserve figure booked ahead of the memo is an exception.
Where booked reserves differ from the actuarial central estimate, confirm the difference is disclosed and explained in the memo.
testing.done: reserve lines agree to a memo dated before Jurat signature and the underlying claims data reconciles to the claims platform extract.

testing.step: Re-run the NAIC cross-check and validation edits independently
actions: Open the filed blank in the statutory reporting software in read-only mode and re-run the full validation suite.
Compare your error and warning list to the final validation report Finance retained; any hit present in yours and absent in theirs is an exception.
Read each retained warning explanation and confirm it names the amount and a substantive reason rather than restating the edit.
Capture your validation output into the workpaper as evidence.
testing.done: the independent validation run shows zero errors and every retained warning carries a substantive, amount-specific explanation.

testing.step: Recompute the three balancing ties and the surplus roll-forward
actions: Recompute Page 2 Line 28 net admitted assets against Page 3 total liabilities plus capital and surplus.

Recompute the capital and surplus roll-forward: prior-quarter surplus + net income + change in nonadmitted + change in net deferred tax + change in provision for reinsurance − dividends, and compare to the reported ending surplus.
Recompute the Page 5 net change in cash against the movement in the Page 2 cash, cash equivalents and short-term investment lines.
Compare the year-to-date Page 4 columns to the prior-quarter filed blank plus the quarter movement, and the prior-year comparatives to the filed Annual Blank.
testing.done: all three ties reconcile to the dollar and the year-to-date roll from the prior filed blank is proved.

testing.step: Verify the Jurat identifiers, signatures and the 45-day readiness date
actions: Check the NAIC company code, FEIN and state of domicile on the Jurat against the company's certificate of authority and the NAIC company listing.
Compare the officer and director list to the latest board minutes held by the Corporate Secretary and flag any stale name.
Confirm the required officer signatures are present, dated, and notarised where the domiciliary state demands it.
Recompute the 45-day deadline from quarter end (March 31 → May 15, June 30 → August 14, September 30 → November 14) and confirm the Jurat date precedes the internal 5-business-day buffer.
testing.done: Jurat identifiers match the certificate of authority, the director list matches board minutes, and the signature date precedes the recomputed internal cut-off.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the company, blank page and line, the dollar difference and the effect on reported capital and surplus.
Assign a root cause — unmapped new GL account, missed SAP adjustment, late subledger posting, stale reserve data, overridden cross-check — and an owner in Finance.
Set a remediation date and, for any misstatement above 0.5% of capital and surplus, open an amended-blank assessment with the Controller and the CFO.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a tracker issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the aggregate misstatement as a percentage of capital and surplus and compare it to the 0.5% fail threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and reviewed no page of the blank and does not report to the Controller for this engagement, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any amended-blank recommendation to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the aggregate misstatement percentage, a conclusion against the 0.5% threshold and the Audit Committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Rebuild the jurisdiction filing matrix from the license register and the state checklists
actions: Extract from the license register every jurisdiction in which each writing company holds an active certificate of authority as at quarter end, including any licence surrendered or added during the quarter.

Open the state filing checklists in the current-year NAIC Quarterly Statement Instructions and, for each jurisdiction, record: electronic-only or PDF or hard copy, number of copies, notarisation requirement, filing fee amount and payment method, and any state-specific supplement.
Flag the domiciliary state row — it drives the primary filing and any state-specific cover letter.
Send the matrix to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for confirmation before any filing is made, and record their approval date.
checklist.done: the matrix lists every licensed jurisdiction with its channel, copy count, fee and supplement, approved by the Regulatory Reporting Manager.

checklist.step: Confirm licence status changes so no jurisdiction is over- or under-filed
actions: Compare this quarter's licensed-jurisdiction list to last quarter's and list every addition and removal.
For each addition, confirm the certificate of authority effective date precedes quarter end so the first filing obligation is correctly dated.
For each removal, obtain the state's written acknowledgement of withdrawal and confirm whether a final statement is still required.
Record each change with its evidence document reference on the matrix row.
checklist.done: every licence addition and removal is evidenced and its first or final filing obligation is stated on the matrix row.

checklist.step: Verify NAIC and state portal filing credentials before the filing window opens
actions: By day 20 after quarter end, log in to NAIC iSite+ and confirm the company's Financial Data Repository filing access is active for the statement year and quarter and the filer account is neither locked nor expired.
Walk the jurisdiction matrix and test the login for every state filing portal used last quarter; reset any expired password now rather than on filing day, and record the reset date on the matrix row.
Confirm with the Accounts Payable Specialist that the EFT banking details for state fee payments are unchanged and that the NAIC filing fee invoice for the statement year has been received.

Record on the matrix any state that changed its portal URL, submission email or transmittal form since last quarter, citing the state bulletin or current-year checklist entry that announced the change.
Report readiness to the Regulatory Reporting Manager by day 22 with every unresolved access issue named and owned.
checklist.done: NAIC Financial Data Repository access and every state portal credential is verified working by day 20, with changed submission channels recorded and sourced on the matrix.

checklist.step: Generate the NAIC electronic filing file from the signed blank
actions: In the statutory reporting software open the signed quarterly blank and run the Electronic Filing export for the NAIC filing type (Quarterly Statement).
Confirm the export header carries the correct NAIC company code, statement year, quarter and company type before it is written.
Run the pre-submission edit check the software applies to the export and clear every hard error.
Produce the print-image PDF of the full blank in parallel for the states that take PDF rather than the electronic file.
Hand the export file and the PDF to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with the file hash noted so the filed version is provable.
checklist.done: a clean electronic filing file and a matching print-image PDF exist for the correct company code, year and quarter, with the file hash recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the electronic filing to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's filing credentials and open the Financial Data Repository filing upload for the statement year and quarter.
Select filing type Quarterly Statement, attach the electronic filing file and submit for the correct NAIC company code.
Wait for the NAIC processing result and read the returned validation report rather than assuming acceptance on upload.
Save the NAIC confirmation, its submission date/time and the confirmation reference into the filing register.
Where the NAIC returns errors, correct in the statutory reporting software, regenerate and re-submit the same day.
checklist.done: the NAIC returns an accepted status for the company code, year and quarter, and the confirmation reference and timestamp are in the filing register.

checklist.step: File with the domiciliary state and capture its acknowledgement
actions: Follow the domiciliary state's own instruction — for Alaska, submit through the Division of Insurance's designated filing channel with the signed Jurat page and any required cover letter.
Attach the state-specific items the checklist demands: signed Jurat, notarised page where required, and the state's transmittal or certification form.
Pay the domiciliary filing fee by the method the checklist specifies and record the payment reference.
Request and file the state's acknowledgement; where the state does not auto-acknowledge, email the financial analyst named on the state's website and file the reply.
checklist.done: the domiciliary state filing is submitted with the required signed and notarised pages, the fee is paid and an acknowledgement is on file.

checklist.step: Work the electronic-only jurisdictions in a single controlled pass
actions: Filter the matrix to jurisdictions whose checklist states the NAIC electronic filing satisfies the state requirement with no separate submission.
For each, confirm the state's checklist entry for the current statement year still reads electronic-only — states move off this each year.
Record on the matrix row the checklist page or bulletin relied on and the date it was read.
Mark each row Filed-via-NAIC with the NAIC confirmation reference carried across as the evidence.
checklist.done: every electronic-only jurisdiction row cites a current-year checklist source and carries the NAIC confirmation reference as its evidence.

checklist.step: Submit the PDF and portal jurisdictions state by state
actions: For each jurisdiction requiring its own submission, open the state's insurance department filing portal or the filing email address named in the checklist.
Upload or attach the print-image PDF plus the state-specific supplement the checklist lists, naming the file <NAIC code>-<year>-Q<n>-<state>.pdf.
Complete any state cover sheet or transmittal fields — company name, NAIC code, FEIN, statement period, contact name and phone.
Capture the portal confirmation screen or the delivery receipt to PDF and file it against the matrix row before moving to the next state.
Work the list in matrix order and never batch-close rows without an individual confirmation.
checklist.done: every PDF or portal jurisdiction has an individual, captured confirmation filed against its matrix row.

checklist.step: Handle the hard-copy and notarised-original jurisdictions
actions: Print the number of copies each remaining checklist demands and attach the notarised original Jurat where the state requires a wet signature.
Send by trackable courier to the address printed in the state's checklist entry, allowing the transit days to land before the 45-day date, not after.
Record the courier tracking number and the guaranteed delivery date on the matrix row.
Confirm delivery from the courier record and file the proof of delivery as the timeliness evidence.
checklist.done: each hard-copy jurisdiction has a courier tracking number and a proof of delivery dated on or before its 45-day deadline.

checklist.step: Pay and evidence every jurisdiction filing fee
actions: Take the fee schedule from the approved jurisdiction matrix and raise the payments in the ERP by the method each state accepts (EFT, state portal card payment, or cheque).
Pay the NAIC filing fee invoice for the statement year against the company's NAIC company code.
Record the payment reference, amount and value date against each matrix row and confirm the value date lands before the state's deadline.
Chase any payment returned or rejected the same day — an unpaid fee can void an otherwise timely filing.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction with a fee has a recorded payment reference and a value date on or before its filing deadline.

checklist.step: Work rejections and state objections to closure
actions: Monitor the filing inbox and the state portals daily through the filing window for rejection notices, validation failures and analyst queries.
Log each rejection as a tracker issue naming the jurisdiction, the stated reason and the original submission date.
Fix the underlying cause with the Statutory Reporting Manager, regenerate the file or PDF and re-submit within 3 business days of the rejection.
Record the re-submission date and the final acceptance, and note whether the original submission date still stands for timeliness.
checklist.done: every rejection is logged, re-submitted within 3 business days and closed with a final acceptance recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing register to the licensed-jurisdiction list before the deadline
actions: On day 40 after quarter end, join the filing register to the licence register and list every licensed jurisdiction with no confirmation.
Chase each gap directly with the analyst who owns the row and require a same-day submission or a written blocker.
Escalate any jurisdiction still unfiled on day 43 to the Controller with the reason and the remediation plan.
Re-run the reconciliation on the deadline date and record the final unfiled count — the target is zero.
checklist.done: the day-43 reconciliation shows zero licensed jurisdictions without a confirmation, or each gap is escalated in writing to the Controller.

checklist.step: Escalate and self-report any jurisdiction that will miss its 45-day date
actions: Where a jurisdiction cannot be filed by its statutory date, notify the Controller and the CFO in writing on the same business day with the cause and the expected filing date.
Contact the state's financial analyst before the deadline passes to request an extension where the state's statute allows one, and record the request and reply.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any written explanation or extension request that admits a missed statutory deadline before it is sent.
Record the state's response, any penalty assessed and the payment status on the tracker issue.
checklist.done: every at-risk jurisdiction has a same-day written escalation, a counsel-reviewed communication to the state and a recorded state response.

checklist.step: Archive the submission confirmations as the timeliness evidence set
actions: File under company / year / quarter: the NAIC Financial Data Repository confirmation, each state acknowledgement or portal receipt, courier proofs of delivery, fee payment records and the filed PDF with its file hash.
Name each confirmation <state>-Q<n>-<year>-confirmation so a jurisdiction can be produced on request without a search.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the filing date.
Confirm the repository index makes the set searchable by NAIC company code, jurisdiction and quarter.
checklist.done: a complete, per-jurisdiction confirmation set is archived under a 7-year label and retrievable by company code, jurisdiction and quarter.

checklist.step: Report filing completion to the Controller and to the Audit Committee pack
actions: Produce the quarter's filing scorecard: jurisdictions licensed, jurisdictions filed, filed-on-time percentage, rejections and re-submissions, fees paid.
Send the scorecard to the Controller within 5 business days of the 45-day deadline with the exception list attached.
Add the scorecard to the Audit Committee reporting pack for the next sitting.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's opening agenda.
checklist.done: a filing scorecard with the on-time percentage and open exceptions is issued to the Controller within 5 business days of the deadline.

testing.step: Build the population from the licence register, not the filing log
actions: Extract every active certificate of authority per writing company as at quarter end from the licence register.
Cross-check the count against the NAIC company listing for the entity so a state licence missing from the internal register cannot hide.
Expand each licence into one expected filing row per jurisdiction per company for the quarter.
Record the extract timestamp, the expected row count and any register-to-NAIC difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: the expected-filing population is built from the licence register, cross-checked to the NAIC company listing, with the row count recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filing register and list the gaps
actions: Join the expected-filing rows to the filing register on company code + jurisdiction + quarter.
List every expected row with no matching register entry as an automatic exception.
List every register entry with no expected row — an unlicensed jurisdiction filing signals a stale licence record.
Resolve the direction of each difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every expected filing is matched to a register entry or listed as an exception, and unexpected filings are explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of jurisdiction filings
actions: Take 100% of the domiciliary state, the NAIC Financial Data Repository submission, every hard-copy jurisdiction and every jurisdiction with a rejection logged in the quarter.
Draw 20 further jurisdictions at random from the remainder using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and resulting coverage percentage in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least one jurisdiction from each submission channel — electronic-only, portal, PDF-by-email and hard copy.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the domiciliary state, all hard-copy and rejected jurisdictions and every submission channel.

testing.step: Re-perform confirmation lookup in the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the Financial Data Repository filing history for the company's NAIC code, statement year and quarter.
Confirm the filing shows an accepted status and read the recorded submission date/time from the NAIC record itself, not from the internal register.
Compare the NAIC-recorded date to the date in the filing register; any difference is an exception.
Capture the NAIC filing history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: the NAIC record shows accepted status and its submission date agrees to the filing register, with the screen captured.

testing.step: Trace each sampled jurisdiction to its own acknowledgement and identifiers
actions: Open the archived confirmation for each sampled jurisdiction and check it names the correct company, NAIC code, statement year and quarter.
For hard-copy jurisdictions, open the courier proof of delivery and read the delivered date rather than the despatch date.
For electronic-only jurisdictions, confirm the current-year state checklist entry cited on the matrix row genuinely says the NAIC filing satisfies the state.
Treat a confirmation naming the wrong quarter or the wrong company code as a fail, not a filing-error to be tidied.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an acknowledgement naming the correct company, code, year and quarter, with delivered dates used for hard copy.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day deadline and the days-late count for the whole population
actions: Recompute each jurisdiction's due date as quarter end plus 45 days — March 31 → May 15, June 30 → August 14, September 30 → November 14 — and adjust only where a state statute on the matrix row states otherwise.
Compute days late = confirmation date minus due date for every row and list every positive value.
Where an extension was granted, confirm a written state approval exists and pre-dates the original due date before accepting the revised date.
Compute the on-time percentage across all licensed jurisdictions and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
testing.done: days-late is computed for every jurisdiction, extensions are supported by pre-dated written approvals, and the on-time percentage is stated.

testing.step: Verify fee payment supports the filing where the state requires it
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction with a fee on the matrix, pull the payment record from the ERP and read the amount and value date.
Compare the amount paid to the fee in the state's current-year checklist entry and flag under- or over-payments.
Confirm the value date is on or before the state's due date.
Flag any returned or reversed payment as an exception even where the filing itself was acknowledged.
testing.done: each sampled fee agrees to the state checklist amount and was value-dated on or before the due date, with reversals flagged.

testing.step: Re-perform the rejection and re-submission handling
actions: Pull every rejection issue raised in the quarter and read the original submission date, the rejection date and the re-submission date.
Compute the re-submission turnaround and flag anything over 3 business days.
Confirm the root cause recorded on the issue is substantive (wrong file format, missing notarised page, wrong company code) rather than 'state rejected'.
Confirm the final acceptance is evidenced and whether the state treated the original date as the filing date.
testing.done: every rejection shows a substantive root cause, a turnaround within 3 business days and an evidenced final acceptance.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per late, missing or unconfirmed jurisdiction naming the company, jurisdiction, due date, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause — stale licence record, wrong submission channel on the matrix, unpaid fee, missed courier transit, unworked rejection — and an owner in Regulatory Reporting.
For any jurisdiction filed after its statutory date, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and record any penalty exposure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for late filings, a counsel self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: State the on-time filing percentage across all licensed jurisdictions and compare it to the zero-late-jurisdiction threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper reference for each late or missing jurisdiction.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted none of the filings and drew the jurisdiction list from the licence register, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late-filing exposure to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time percentage, the conclusion against the zero-late threshold and the Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the supplemental schedule and exhibit set; the Statutory Reporting Manager builds them and the Appointed Actuary owns Schedule P and the reserve-related exhibits

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska financial reporting statute (rep jurisdiction) with the Alabama, Arizona and California financial reporting statutes, read against the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental filing index and the AP&P Manual SSAPs governing each schedule

In-scope processes.value: Preparation of the schedules and exhibits accompanying the blank: Schedules A/B/BA/D/DA/DB/E (investments), Schedule F (reinsurance), Schedule P (loss development), Schedule T (premiums and losses by state), Schedule Y (holding company), the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses state pages, Five-Year Historical Data, the Insurance Expense Exhibit and the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit

In-scope systems.value: Schedules are built in the statutory reporting software from the investment accounting system, the ceded accounting platform, the policy administration premium register and the reserving platform triangles

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supplemental Schedules and Exhibits Procedure — one section per schedule naming the source system, the extract, the cross-check to the blank page it must tie to, the preparer and the reviewer

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and re-approved each January against the new-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental index, which adds and retires schedules year to year

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly schedules (Schedule F, Schedule Y Part 1A, investment verification pages) travel with the blank by the 45-day date; the annual schedule set is due with the Annual Blank by March 1, the Insurance Expense Exhibit by April 1 and the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit by March 1

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar tasks per schedule: source extract due at quarter-end +12, draft schedule at +25, cross-check clearance at +32; annual-only schedules carry January 20 / February 10 / February 20 milestones ahead of March 1

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each schedule with its source extract, the tie-out worksheet to the blank page, and the preparer/reviewer sign-off grid retained 7 years from the filing date in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any schedule that fails its cross-check to the blank, any omitted supplemental filing from the instructions index, and any schedule filed without its source extract on file is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs off every schedule correction and every decision that a listed supplemental filing is not applicable to the company

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full supplemental filing index from the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions expanded per writing company, plus every line of the investment, reinsurance and state-premium schedules for the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every schedule must tie to its blank page to the dollar; any omitted applicable supplemental filing, any Schedule T state premium differing from the state page, or any Schedule F reinsurer without a valid NAIC code is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Quarterly schedules tested each quarter alongside the blank; the annual-only set (Schedule P, Insurance Expense Exhibit, Five-Year Historical, Supplemental Compensation Exhibit) tested once ahead of the March 1 annual filing

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have prepared no schedule under test and must pull source extracts independently of Finance

Evidence location for test results.value: Supplemental schedule test workpaper (instructions index completeness check, per-schedule tie-out, sampled line re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Schedule set with source extracts and tie-out worksheets, presentable to a domiciliary financial examiner or an NAIC analyst inquiry within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Statutory Reporting Manager answers schedule-level analyst queries; the Appointed Actuary answers Schedule P development questions; the Controller clears any schedule restatement before it is sent

checklist.step: Rebuild the applicable supplemental filing index for the company
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental filing index and list every schedule, exhibit and supplement named for the company type.
Mark each entry Applicable or Not Applicable and, for every Not Applicable, write the reason (line of business not written, threshold not met, product not sold).
Compare the index to last year's list and highlight every added and retired filing so nothing carries forward on autopilot.
Have the Controller approve the Not Applicable determinations in writing before the schedules are built.
checklist.done: the index shows an Applicable/Not Applicable decision for every entry, with reasons, approved in writing by the Controller.

checklist.step: Build the investment schedules from the investment accounting extract
actions: Extract the holdings file at period end with CUSIP, description, acquisition date, par, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value, NAIC designation and interest/dividend received.

Populate Schedule D Part 1 (bonds) and Part 2 (stocks), Schedule DA (short-term), Schedule DB (derivatives), Schedule E (cash and deposits), Schedule A (real estate) and Schedule B (mortgage loans) from that single extract.
Confirm every bond carries a current NAIC designation from the Securities Valuation Office or an approved filing-exempt rating, and list any security without one.
Prove the Schedule D summary by category ties to the Page 2 invested asset lines to the dollar.
Hand the extract and the tie-out to the Statutory Reporting Manager with the extract timestamp.
checklist.done: the investment schedules tie to the Page 2 invested asset lines to the dollar and every bond carries a NAIC designation or is listed as an exception.

checklist.step: Build Schedule F from the ceded reinsurance ledger
actions: Extract by reinsurer: ceded premiums, paid and unpaid loss recoverables, ceded unearned premium, contingent commissions, funds held and collateral held (letters of credit, trust, funds withheld).
Populate Schedule F Part 3 with each reinsurer's NAIC company code, ID number, domiciliary jurisdiction and authorized / unauthorized / certified / reciprocal status as at period end.
Age the recoverable balances and compute the overdue amounts that drive the provision for reinsurance in Schedule F Part 3 penalty columns.
Confirm each collateral figure against the letter of credit register and the trust statements held by Treasury.
Tie the total ceded recoverable to the Page 2 and Page 3 reinsurance lines and file the reconciliation.
checklist.done: Schedule F carries a NAIC code and status for every reinsurer, aged recoverables driving the provision, and ties to the blank reinsurance lines.

checklist.step: Build Schedule T and the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses state pages
actions: Extract direct written premium, direct earned premium, direct losses paid and direct losses incurred by state of risk from the policy administration and claims platforms for the period.
Populate Schedule T with the by-state allocation and the licence status column for all 51 jurisdictions plus territories.
Populate the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses state page for each jurisdiction from the same extract so the two can never diverge.
Prove the Schedule T direct written premium total equals the Page 4 direct written premium and that each state's figure equals its state page.
List any state showing premium where the company holds no licence and escalate to the Compliance Officer the same day.
checklist.done: Schedule T totals agree to the blank direct premium, each state agrees to its state page, and unlicensed-state premium is escalated.

checklist.step: Build Schedule Y from the current holding company structure
actions: Produce the organisational chart as at period end showing the ultimate controlling person and every affiliate with ownership percentages.
Populate Schedule Y Part 1 (organisational chart) and Part 1A (detail of insurers and their NAIC codes, FEINs and domiciles).
Populate Part 2 with amounts due to and from affiliates for the period and agree them to the intercompany balances in the general ledger.
Confirm any change of control, merger or new subsidiary since the last filing is reflected and cross-referenced to the Form B holding company registration.
Have Legal Counsel confirm the ultimate controlling person disclosure before it is finalised.
checklist.done: Schedule Y shows a current chart with the ultimate controlling person confirmed by Legal Counsel and affiliate balances agreed to the GL.

checklist.step: Build Schedule P from the reserving triangles for the annual filing
actions: Produce the paid loss, case reserve, incurred loss, defense and cost containment and adjusting and other expense triangles by Schedule P line of business at the annual evaluation date.
Populate Schedule P Parts 1 through 4 with the ten-year accident year history, gross and net of reinsurance, and Part 5 claim counts where the line requires them.
Prove the Schedule P Part 1 current-year net incurred total ties to the Page 4 losses incurred and the Part 2 latest diagonal to booked reserves.
Recompute the one-year and two-year development figures and check them against the prior filed Schedule P.
Explain in the workpaper every accident year showing adverse development above 5% of the prior held reserve.
checklist.done: Schedule P ties to the blank incurred and reserve lines, development recomputes against the prior filing, and material adverse years are explained.

checklist.step: Complete the quarterly Schedule P interrogatory and the quarterly reinsurance interrogatories
actions: Answer the quarterly Schedule P interrogatory on the adequacy of the recorded reserve for unpaid losses using the Reserving Actuary's written response.
Answer the reinsurance interrogatories on retroactive reinsurance, financial reinsurance and any contract lacking risk transfer, taking written confirmation from the Reinsurance Manager.
Where any answer changed from the prior quarter, record the change and its cause on the interrogatory support sheet.
Route the reinsurance risk-transfer answers to Legal Counsel where a contract amendment was signed in the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarterly reserve and reinsurance interrogatories are answered from written confirmations, with every change from the prior quarter explained.

checklist.step: Build the Five-Year Historical Data exhibit
actions: Populate the Five-Year Historical Data page from the four prior filed Annual Blanks plus the current year, pulling each prior column from the filed statement rather than from internal restatements.
Compare each prior-year column to the corresponding filed blank and correct any drift; a prior column must never move without a disclosed restatement.
Recompute the derived ratios the exhibit requires (loss ratio, expense ratio, premium to surplus, reserve development) and check them against the current-year pages.
Document any restated prior column with the reason and the Note reference disclosing it.
checklist.done: each prior-year column agrees to the filed blank for that year and every derived ratio recomputes from the current pages.

checklist.step: Build the Insurance Expense Exhibit and allocate expenses by line
actions: Extract the expense ledger by natural account and cost centre for the calendar year and apply the standing allocation bases (headcount, premium volume, claim counts) per the documented allocation methodology.
Populate the Insurance Expense Exhibit Parts I, II and III allocating loss adjustment, other underwriting and investment expenses by line of business.
Prove the exhibit's total expenses equal the Page 4 underwriting and investment expense lines to the dollar.
Have the FP&A Manager confirm the allocation bases used for the year and file the confirmation.
Diarise the filing for April 1, separately from the March 1 Annual Blank.
checklist.done: the Insurance Expense Exhibit ties to the Page 4 expense totals, allocation bases are confirmed by FP&A and the April 1 filing is diarised.

checklist.step: Build the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit from payroll records
actions: Extract for the calendar year the compensation of the directors and officers and the other individuals the exhibit instructions require, including salary, bonus and all other compensation.
Reconcile the extracted totals to the payroll ledger posted in the general ledger for the year.
Confirm the individual list against the Jurat officer and director listing and the board minutes held by the Corporate Secretary.
Route the exhibit to the Chief HR Officer and the Controller for confidentiality review before it is added to the filing set, and diarise the March 1 filing.
checklist.done: the compensation exhibit reconciles to payroll, covers the Jurat officer and director list, and is reviewed before the March 1 filing.

checklist.step: Run the schedule-to-blank cross-checks and clear every break
actions: Run the statutory reporting software's schedule cross-check suite covering Schedule D to Page 2, Schedule F to the reinsurance lines, Schedule T to Page 4 direct premium, Schedule P to losses incurred, and the state pages to Schedule T.
Work every break to zero and record on the tie-out worksheet the amount, the cause and the correction for each one cleared.
Where a break cannot be cleared without restating a source system, escalate to the Controller rather than plugging the schedule.
Export the final clean cross-check report as the evidence for the schedule set.
checklist.done: the cross-check report is clean and the tie-out worksheet records amount, cause and correction for every break cleared.

checklist.step: Obtain per-schedule preparer and reviewer sign-off
actions: Maintain a sign-off grid with one row per schedule showing source system, extract timestamp, preparer, reviewer and tie-out reference.
Confirm no schedule has the same person as preparer and reviewer.
Review the analytical commentary on every schedule with a period-over-period movement above 10% and require an explanation before signing.
Sign the grid to release the schedule set into the filing package.
checklist.done: the sign-off grid is complete with distinct preparer and reviewer per schedule and is signed by the Controller.

checklist.step: Route the actuarial schedules to the Appointed Actuary for confirmation
actions: Read Schedule P, the reserve-related interrogatories and the reserve lines of the blank against the reserve analysis supporting the opinion.
Confirm in writing that the schedules reflect the reserves the opinion covers, naming the evaluation date and any difference.
Raise to the Controller any presentation in the schedules that would be inconsistent with the Statement of Actuarial Opinion and the Actuarial Opinion Summary.
Date and file the confirmation with the schedule set before the filing package closes.
checklist.done: a dated written confirmation from the Appointed Actuary ties Schedule P and the reserve lines to the reserves the opinion covers.

checklist.step: Assemble the schedule set into the filing package and hand it to Regulatory Reporting
actions: Confirm every Applicable entry on the supplemental filing index is present in the package and every Not Applicable entry carries its approved reason.
Attach the schedules to the blank in the statutory reporting software so the electronic filing export carries them.
Note separately the supplements filed on their own dates (Insurance Expense Exhibit April 1, Supplemental Compensation Exhibit March 1) so they are not lost after the main filing.
Hand the package to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the index and the sign-off grid attached.
checklist.done: the package contains every Applicable schedule, the index, the sign-off grid, and separately-dated supplements are diarised.

checklist.step: Archive each schedule with its source extract and tie-out
actions: File per schedule: the filed schedule, the source system extract with its timestamp, the tie-out worksheet and the sign-off row.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the filing date so the set survives a full financial examination cycle.
Index by schedule name, NAIC company code, statement year and period so an examiner request for 'Schedule F Part 3' resolves in one search.
Send the Controller the archive link as the close-out for the schedule set.
checklist.done: every schedule is archived with its dated source extract and tie-out under a 7-year label, indexed by schedule name and period.

testing.step: Build the population from the NAIC supplemental filing index
actions: Take the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplemental filing index directly rather than the company's copy and list every entry for the company type.
Expand it per writing company into an expected-schedule population.
Mark each entry with the company's Applicable/Not Applicable determination and the recorded reason.
Record the index edition, the extraction date and the expected-schedule count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the expected-schedule population is built from the NAIC index itself with the company's applicability decision attached to each row.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed schedule set to the expected population
actions: Join the expected-schedule rows to the schedules actually present in the filed package.
List every Applicable entry with no filed schedule as an automatic exception.
Challenge every Not Applicable determination against the company's actual lines of business, premium volume and product set — a Not Applicable that is contradicted by Schedule T premium is a fail.
Confirm the separately-dated supplements (Insurance Expense Exhibit, Supplemental Compensation Exhibit) were filed on their own dates and are not merely diarised.
testing.done: every Applicable schedule is present, every Not Applicable is defensible against actual business written, and separately-dated supplements are evidenced as filed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of schedule lines
actions: Take 100% of Schedule F reinsurers with unauthorized or certified status, all Schedule T states with premium above 5% of direct written premium, and all Schedule P lines with adverse development above 5%.
Draw 25 Schedule D holdings and 15 further Schedule T states at random using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, the population sizes per schedule, the selection date and the coverage percentage.
Confirm the sample spans investment, reinsurance, state-premium and loss-development schedules.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers unauthorized reinsurers, major premium states, adversely developing lines and a random spread of holdings.

testing.step: Re-perform the investment schedule build from an independent extract
actions: Pull the period-end holdings file directly from the investment accounting system rather than taking Finance's extract.
For each sampled holding compare CUSIP, par, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value and NAIC designation to the Schedule D line.
Recompute the Schedule D category subtotals and compare them to the Page 2 invested asset lines.
List any bond without a current NAIC designation or filing-exempt rating as an exception with its carrying value.
testing.done: sampled Schedule D lines agree to an independently pulled holdings file and the category subtotals recompute to Page 2.

testing.step: Re-perform Schedule F reinsurer status and the provision computation
actions: For each sampled reinsurer, verify the NAIC company code and the authorized / certified / reciprocal status against the domiciliary state's approved list as at period end.
Re-age the recoverable balances from the ceded ledger and recompute the overdue amounts driving the Schedule F penalty columns.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance and compare it to the Page 3 line.
Trace each sampled collateral figure to the letter of credit register or the trust statement and flag any collateral that expired before period end.
testing.done: reinsurer statuses verify against the state's approved list, the re-aged provision recomputes to the Page 3 line and collateral traces to live instruments.

testing.step: Re-perform the Schedule T state allocation against the premium register
actions: Pull direct written and earned premium by state of risk from the policy administration premium register for the period.
Compare each sampled state to its Schedule T line and to its Exhibit of Premiums and Losses state page — all three must agree.
Recompute the Schedule T total and compare it to the blank's direct written premium line.
Cross-check the licence status column against the licence register and flag any state showing premium without an active licence.
testing.done: each sampled state agrees across the premium register, Schedule T and its state page, and no premium sits in an unlicensed state.

testing.step: Recompute the Schedule P development and Five-Year Historical continuity
actions: Recompute the one-year and two-year loss development from the current and prior filed Schedule P and compare to the reported figures.
Tie the Schedule P Part 1 current-year net incurred total to the blank losses incurred line.
Compare each prior-year column of the Five-Year Historical Data page to the corresponding filed Annual Blank and list every drift.
Treat any moved prior-year column with no disclosed restatement Note as an exception.
testing.done: development recomputes to the reported figures and every Five-Year Historical prior column agrees to its filed blank or carries a disclosed restatement.

testing.step: Verify the expense allocation behind the Insurance Expense Exhibit
actions: Pull the year's expense ledger by natural account and cost centre and recompute the allocation to line of business using the documented bases.
Compare the recomputed allocation to the exhibit's Parts I, II and III by line.
Confirm the exhibit total equals the blank's underwriting and investment expense lines.
Flag any allocation basis applied without the FP&A Manager's written confirmation for the year.
testing.done: the recomputed allocation agrees to the exhibit by line, the total ties to the blank and every basis has written FP&A confirmation.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the schedule, the line or reinsurer or state, the dollar difference and the blank line affected.
Assign a root cause — stale source extract, unmapped new holding, reinsurer status not refreshed, allocation basis changed without approval, omitted supplemental filing — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a filed schedule is wrong, open an amended-schedule assessment with the Controller.
Carry every open exception into the next period's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a schedule reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amended-schedule decision where the filing is wrong.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: State the number of schedules failing their tie-out and the aggregate dollar difference against the tie-to-the-dollar threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each failed schedule.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no schedule and pulled source extracts independently of Finance, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any omitted supplemental filing to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the failed-schedule count, the aggregate difference, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the annual audited statutory financial report and the auditor relationship; the Audit Committee owns the appointment and the independence determination

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska financial reporting statute (rep jurisdiction) with Alabama, Arizona and California financial reporting statutes, read alongside each state's adoption of the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205) governing the audited report, auditor qualification and internal control communication

In-scope processes.value: Annual audit lifecycle for every licensed writing company: auditor appointment and independence determination → Audit Committee oversight → PBC delivery and fieldwork → audited statutory financial report with the auditor's opinion → filing with the domiciliary state and all 51 jurisdictions → internal control communication and management's ICFR report

In-scope systems.value: Audited report drafted from the filed Annual Blank held in the statutory reporting software; PBC evidence, auditor correspondence and the signed opinion held in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Audit Coordination Procedure — auditor appointment and 5-year lead partner rotation check, independence confirmation, Audit Committee calendar, PBC ownership, audited-report-to-blank reconciliation, filing and the internal control communication

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee chair and re-approved annually at the meeting that appoints the auditor for the coming year

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Audited statutory financial report due June 1 following the December 31 year end; the accountant's Communication of Internal Control Related Matters Noted in an Audit due August 1; Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting due August 1 where the premium threshold is met; the auditor appointment notice due within the model-regulation notice window

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit calendar reminders at December 1 (auditor confirmed and independence letter received), February 15 (PBC complete), April 15 (draft report circulated), May 20 (opinion signed), and July 15 (internal control communication)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement letter, independence and lead-partner-rotation confirmations, Audit Committee minutes, signed auditor's opinion, audited report, the audited-to-blank surplus reconciliation and the internal control communication retained 7 years from the June 1 filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed June 1 or August 1 date, an unresolved independence issue, an unfiled auditor appointment notice, or an unreconciled difference between audited surplus and filed Annual Blank surplus is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every audit adjustment affecting filed statutory surplus and any extension request to a state; the Audit Committee chair signs off any auditor independence remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every licensed writing company subject to the audited report requirement, its audit deliverables (opinion, audited report, internal control communication, management's ICFR report) and the jurisdiction filing rows for each deliverable

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the June 1 and August 1 dates and on the audited-surplus-to-blank-surplus reconciliation; any unexplained surplus difference, any missing independence confirmation, or any jurisdiction without the audited report on file is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test runs once after the June 1 filing over 100% of licensed entities and jurisdictions, with an interim independence and appointment check each December

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the Controller's organisation and must not have prepared any audit deliverable or PBC item under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual statutory audit compliance workpaper (entity population, deliverable checklist, filing evidence, surplus reconciliation, independence confirmations, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Audited statutory financial report with the signed opinion, the audited-to-blank reconciliation, the internal control communication and per-jurisdiction filing confirmations, producible for a domiciliary financial examination within 10 business days
