checklist.step: Confirm the auditor appointment and file the appointment notice with the states
actions: Take the Audit Committee resolution appointing the independent certified public accountant for the year and record the firm name, engagement partner and appointment date.
Confirm the firm is registered and in good standing with the state board of accountancy in the domiciliary jurisdiction.

File the auditor appointment notice with the domiciliary state within the notice window its adoption of the Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation requires, and copy the other licensed jurisdictions where required.
Where an auditor is dismissed or resigns, file the required notification and the statement of any disagreement within the state's window and log the date.
checklist.done: the appointment resolution, the good-standing check and the state appointment notices are on file with their filing dates recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain the auditor independence and lead-partner-rotation confirmation
actions: Request the firm's written independence confirmation addressed to the Audit Committee, covering the firm, the engagement partner and the concurring reviewer for the audit year.
Check the lead and concurring partner have not served more than the five consecutive years the model regulation permits, and record the year count for each.
List every non-audit service the firm provided in the year and check each against the prohibited-service list; obtain Audit Committee pre-approval evidence for the permitted ones.
Escalate any prohibited service or rotation breach to the Audit Committee chair before fieldwork starts, not after.
checklist.done: a written independence confirmation is on file with partner-year counts inside the five-year limit and every non-audit service pre-approved.

checklist.step: Agree the engagement letter, scope and audit timetable
actions: Review the engagement letter for the statutory basis of accounting (NAIC AP&P Manual), the entities covered, the reporting deliverables and the workpaper access clause the model regulation requires for state examiners.
Agree the timetable against the June 1 filing date working back: fieldwork start, PBC delivery dates, draft report date and opinion signing date.
Confirm the agreed materiality and the planned scope with the Audit Committee before signing.
Execute the letter through the contract system and file the signed copy with the audit evidence.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter names the statutory basis, the entities, the workpaper access clause and a timetable that lands before June 1.

checklist.step: Build and own the prepared-by-client (PBC) list
actions: Take the auditor's PBC request list and assign every item an internal owner, a source system and a due date ahead of fieldwork.
Load the list into a shared PBC tracker with status per item and a single upload location the auditor can access.
Chase items at their due date and escalate anything more than 3 business days late to the Controller — late PBC is the usual cause of a late opinion.
Log every auditor request received after the list is closed as a supplementary item with its own owner and date.
checklist.done: every PBC item has an owner, a due date and a delivered status, with late items escalated and supplementary requests tracked.

checklist.step: Support fieldwork with the statutory close evidence already produced
actions: Give the auditor the completed year-end account reconciliations from the close tool with preparer and reviewer sign-offs visible.
Provide the frozen trial balance, the GAAP-to-SAP surplus bridge and the SAP adjustment support behind the filed Annual Blank.
Coordinate confirmations the auditor sends to custodians, reinsurers and banks, and chase non-responses weekly.
Answer auditor queries through a single logged channel so every question and answer is retrievable, rather than by ad-hoc email.
checklist.done: reconciliations, the surplus bridge and confirmations are delivered, and every auditor query is logged with its answer.

checklist.step: Resolve audit adjustments and re-tie surplus to the filed Annual Blank
actions: Take the auditor's summary of adjusted and unadjusted differences and assess each against the agreed materiality.
Post the adjustments management accepts to the statutory ledger with the SSAP reference and the audit reference on the journal.
Rebuild the surplus reconciliation: capital and surplus per the filed Annual Blank + audit adjustments = capital and surplus per the audited report, and explain every reconciling item.
Where an adjustment changes filed statutory surplus, take the CFO's decision on whether an amended Annual Blank is required and record it.
File the summary of unadjusted differences with the passed-adjustment rationale.
checklist.done: the audited surplus reconciles to the filed Annual Blank surplus with every adjustment explained and an amended-blank decision recorded.

checklist.step: Take the audited statutory financial report through Audit Committee review
actions: Circulate through the board portal the draft audited statutory financial report — balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, changes in capital and surplus and the Notes — with the auditor's draft opinion.
Present to the Audit Committee the significant accounting estimates, the audit adjustments, the unadjusted differences and any control deficiency raised.
Have the auditor meet the Audit Committee without management present, as the model regulation contemplates, and have the fact minuted.
Record the Audit Committee's approval of the report in the minutes with the meeting date.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has reviewed the draft report with the auditor, met without management, and minuted its approval with a date.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed auditor's opinion and the management representation letter
actions: Sign the management representation letter dated the same day as the auditor's opinion, covering the statutory basis, the completeness of records and subsequent events.
Confirm the auditor's opinion names the statutory basis of accounting prescribed by the domiciliary state insurance department, not US GAAP.
Read the opinion for any qualification, emphasis-of-matter or going-concern paragraph and brief the Audit Committee chair immediately if one is present.
File the signed opinion and representation letter with the audited report in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: a signed opinion on the statutory basis and a same-dated representation letter are on file, with any qualification escalated.

checklist.step: File the audited report with the domiciliary state by June 1
actions: Submit the audited statutory financial report with the signed opinion to the domiciliary insurance department through the channel its filing instructions specify, on or before June 1 following the December 31 year end.
Upload the audited report to the NAIC Financial Data Repository where the filing instructions require it for the statement year.
Capture the submission confirmation and file it against the entity row in the filing register.
Where an extension is needed, request it from the domiciliary commissioner in writing before June 1 with the reason and the proposed date, and have Regulatory Counsel review the request.
checklist.done: the domiciliary June 1 submission is confirmed, or a written pre-deadline extension request reviewed by counsel is on file.

checklist.step: File the audited report with every other licensed jurisdiction
actions: Take the licensed-jurisdiction list per entity and, for each, read that state's audited-report filing requirement — some accept the NAIC filing, others require a direct submission and a filing fee.
Submit through each state's portal or filing address and record the confirmation against the jurisdiction row.
Where a state requires the auditor's awareness letter or a copy of the engagement letter, attach it as that state's checklist demands.
Reconcile the jurisdiction filing register to the licence register before June 1 and chase every gap.
checklist.done: every licensed jurisdiction shows either an accepted direct submission or a documented reliance on the NAIC filing, reconciled before June 1.

checklist.step: Obtain and act on the accountant's internal control communication
actions: Request from the auditor the Communication of Internal Control Related Matters Noted in an Audit, describing any unremediated material weakness in internal control over statutory financial reporting.
File it with the domiciliary state and the other jurisdictions that require it by August 1 following the year end.
For each matter raised, agree a remediation action, an owner and a target date with the process owner and log it.
Report the matters and the remediation plan to the Audit Committee at its next meeting.
checklist.done: the internal control communication is received, filed by August 1, and every matter has an owned, dated remediation action reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Determine whether Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting is required and produce it
actions: Compute the entity's direct written and assumed premium for the year and compare it to the threshold in the state's adoption of the model regulation that triggers the management ICFR report.
Where the threshold is met, document management's assessment of internal control over statutory financial reporting as of December 31, naming the framework used and the controls tested.
Where the entity relies on a parent's Sarbanes-Oxley Section 404 report as the permitted alternative, document the reliance basis and attach the parent report.
File the report or the reliance documentation by August 1 and record the confirmation.
checklist.done: the threshold computation is documented and either a management ICFR report or a documented reliance alternative is filed by August 1.

checklist.step: Assess exemption and hardship relief where an entity qualifies
actions: For each small entity, compute direct written and assumed premium and policyholder counts against the exemption thresholds in each state's adoption of the model regulation.
Where an exemption or a financial-hardship exemption is available, prepare the written request to the commissioner with the supporting figures before the June 1 date.
Record the commissioner's written response and the period it covers on the entity row — an exemption is never assumed from silence.
Re-test the thresholds each year; an exemption granted once does not carry forward automatically.
checklist.done: every claimed exemption rests on a computed threshold and a written commissioner response covering the audit year.

checklist.step: Archive the full audit evidence set
actions: File under entity / audit year: engagement letter, independence and rotation confirmations, Audit Committee minutes, PBC tracker, summary of adjusted and unadjusted differences, signed opinion, audited report, representation letter, surplus reconciliation, internal control communication and every filing confirmation.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the June 1 filing date.
Index by NAIC company code and audit year so an examiner request resolves in one search.
Send the Audit Committee chair the archive link as the close-out of the audit year.
checklist.done: the complete audit evidence set is archived under a 7-year label and retrievable by NAIC company code and audit year.

checklist.step: Close the audit year with a lessons-learned and next-year timetable
actions: Review with the auditor and the Statutory Reporting Manager which PBC items ran late, which adjustments recurred from the prior year and which controls the auditor flagged.
Turn each into an action with an owner and a date in the next close calendar.
Set the next audit year's timetable working back from June 1 and load it into the audit calendar with the December 1, February 15, April 15 and May 20 milestones.
Present the plan to the Audit Committee at the meeting that appoints the next year's auditor.
checklist.done: recurring adjustments and late PBC items are converted into owned actions and the next year's timetable is loaded and presented to the committee.

testing.step: Build the population of entities and required audit deliverables
actions: List every licensed writing company from the licence register with its direct written and assumed premium for the audit year.
For each, derive the required deliverables from each state's adoption of the model regulation: audited report, internal control communication, management ICFR report where the threshold is met.
Mark any entity claiming an exemption and note the claimed basis.
Record the entity count, the deliverable count and the extract date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population lists every entity with its required deliverables derived from premium thresholds, with exemption claims flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the deliverables produced to the deliverables required
actions: Join the required-deliverable rows to the documents actually held in the financial reporting repository for the audit year.
List every required deliverable with no document as an automatic exception.
Recompute each exemption threshold from the entity's premium figures and check a written commissioner response covering the audit year is on file.
Treat an exemption assumed from regulator silence as a fail.
testing.done: every required deliverable is matched to a held document and every exemption rests on a recomputed threshold and a written response.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of entities and filing rows
actions: Take 100% of the domiciliary filings, every entity with an audit adjustment affecting surplus, every entity with a control matter raised and every exemption claim.
Draw 15 further jurisdiction filing rows at random using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the resulting coverage percentage.
Confirm the sample includes at least one entity subject to the management ICFR report.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers domiciliary filings, surplus-affecting adjustments, control matters, exemptions and an ICFR-reporting entity.

testing.step: Re-perform the independence and lead-partner-rotation check
actions: Read the firm's independence confirmation for the audit year and confirm it names the firm, the lead partner and the concurring reviewer.
Count consecutive service years for the lead and concurring partner from the engagement letters of the prior years and compare to the five-year limit.
List every non-audit service invoiced by the firm in the year from the accounts payable ledger and compare it to the prohibited-service list — the invoice ledger, not management's summary.
Confirm Audit Committee pre-approval minutes exist for each permitted non-audit service.
testing.done: partner service years recompute inside the five-year limit and every non-audit service in the AP ledger is permitted and pre-approved.

testing.step: Re-perform the audited-surplus to filed-blank reconciliation
actions: Read capital and surplus from the filed Annual Blank Page 3 and from the audited statutory financial report balance sheet.
Rebuild the reconciliation independently from the posted audit adjustment journals in the general ledger.
Confirm every reconciling item traces to a journal with an audit reference and a SSAP citation.
Any unexplained difference, of any size, is an exception and triggers the amended-blank question.
testing.done: the independently rebuilt reconciliation explains the full difference between audited and filed surplus with every item traced to a journal.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to a dated regulator confirmation
actions: Open the archived confirmation for each sampled jurisdiction and read the submission date from the confirmation itself.
Confirm the confirmation names the correct entity, NAIC company code and audit year.
For jurisdictions relying on the NAIC filing, confirm the state's current filing instruction genuinely permits that reliance and capture the source.
Flag any jurisdiction whose evidence is an internal 'sent' record with no regulator-side acknowledgement.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a regulator-side confirmation naming the right entity, code and audit year, with reliance claims sourced.

testing.step: Recompute the June 1 and August 1 deadline compliance
actions: Compute days late = confirmation date minus June 1 for every audited report filing and minus August 1 for every internal control communication and management ICFR report.
Where an extension was granted, confirm the written commissioner approval pre-dates the original deadline and covers the entity and the deliverable.
Confirm the opinion signature date and the representation letter date precede the filing date.
List every positive days-late value as an exception regardless of magnitude.
testing.done: days-late is computed for every deliverable, extensions are evidenced by pre-dated approvals, and signature dates precede filing dates.

testing.step: Test that control matters raised by the auditor were remediated
actions: List every matter in the accountant's internal control communication and the prior year's communication.
For each, confirm a remediation action with an owner and a target date exists and check the current status against that date.
Test the remediated control by re-performing it for one period and confirming it now operates as described.
Treat any matter repeated from the prior year with no completed remediation as a fail, not an open item.
testing.done: every control matter has an owned, dated remediation and repeat matters with incomplete remediation are recorded as fails.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the deliverable, the jurisdiction and the days late or the dollar difference.
Assign a root cause — late PBC delivery, unresolved audit adjustment, missed appointment notice, partner rotation breach, exemption assumed without a response — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed statutory deadline, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next audit year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for missed deadlines, a counsel self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: State the count of entities and jurisdictions filed on time against the zero-late threshold and the aggregate unexplained surplus difference.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the Controller's organisation and prepared no audit deliverable, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any qualification in the opinion and any unremediated control matter to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states on-time counts, the surplus difference, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the master statutory filing calendar across all 51 jurisdictions; the Regulatory Reporting Analyst maintains the rows and captures the timeliness evidence

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska financial reporting statute (rep jurisdiction) with Alabama, Arizona and California financial reporting statutes, re-read each January against the state filing checklists in the new-year NAIC Annual and Quarterly Statement Instructions and every state financial-reporting bulletin issued during the year

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the statutory filing calendar: jurisdiction and entity matrix upkeep, due-date derivation from the 45-day quarterly rule and the March 1 / April 1 / June 1 / August 1 annual dates, reminder configuration, per-filing confirmation capture and the monthly timeliness reconciliation

In-scope systems.value: Master filing calendar and confirmation register held in the internal regulatory system, fed by the licence register and reconciled to the statutory reporting software's filing history

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Filing Calendar Maintenance Procedure — calendar build from the licence register, due-date derivation rules, quarterly refresh against the NAIC instructions, reminder configuration, evidence capture standard and the monthly unfiled-item reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and re-approved each January when the new-year state filing checklists are published; interim re-approval on any bulletin changing a due date or a channel

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every statutory financial filing per entity per jurisdiction: quarterly blanks at 45 days (May 15, August 14, November 14), Annual Blank and Risk-Based Capital at March 1, Insurance Expense Exhibit at April 1, audited report at June 1, internal control communication at August 1, plus each state's own supplements

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar-driven reminders per row at T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-2 business days to the owner, with an escalation alert to the Regulatory Reporting Manager at T-2 on any row still without a confirmation

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Calendar version history, the confirmation register with every regulator acknowledgement, the monthly reconciliation output and the escalation log retained 7 years from each filing date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A calendar row missing for a licensed jurisdiction, a due date that does not match the state's checklist, a filing with no captured confirmation, or an escalation not actioned at T-2 is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs off every due-date change to the calendar and every closure of a missed-filing exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar row for the period — entity × jurisdiction × filing type — rebuilt independently from the licence register and the current-year NAIC state filing checklists, plus the confirmation register entries

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Calendar completeness must be 100% against the independently rebuilt row set; any missing row, any due date differing from the state checklist, or any filing without a captured regulator confirmation is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the calendar is reconciled monthly by the owner and independently tested quarterly, with an expanded January test after the new-year instructions are published

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the calendar and must rebuild the expected row set from the licence register and the NAIC checklists rather than from the calendar itself

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-calendar completeness workpaper (rebuilt row set, calendar comparison, due-date recomputation, confirmation coverage, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filing calendar export with due dates, actual filing dates and confirmation references per jurisdiction, producible as a timeliness demonstration for a financial examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers examiner and analyst questions on filing history; the Controller clears any explanation of a missed deadline and Regulatory Counsel reviews any communication admitting one

checklist.step: Rebuild the calendar row set from the licence register each January
actions: Extract every active certificate of authority per writing company from the licence register as at January 1 and expand it into one calendar row per entity × jurisdiction × filing type.

Add the filing types from the current-year NAIC Annual and Quarterly Statement Instructions: three quarterly blanks, the Annual Blank, Risk-Based Capital, the Insurance Expense Exhibit, the audited report, the internal control communication and each state's own supplements.
Compare the rebuilt row set to last year's calendar and list every added, retired and changed row.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve the year's row set before any reminder is armed.
checklist.done: the year's calendar is rebuilt from the licence register, differences from last year are listed, and the row set is approved.

checklist.step: Derive and record each row's due date from its own source
actions: For quarterly blank rows compute due date = quarter end + 45 days (March 31 → May 15, June 30 → August 14, September 30 → November 14) and store the computation, not just the result.
For annual rows enter the fixed dates: Annual Blank and Risk-Based Capital March 1, Insurance Expense Exhibit April 1, audited report June 1, internal control communication August 1.
Where a state's checklist or statute sets a different date, override the row and paste the exact source sentence and its citation onto the row.
Record on each row the source document, the page or bulletin reference and the date it was read.
checklist.done: every row shows a due date, the computation or fixed-date rule behind it, and a cited, dated source for any override.

checklist.step: Record the submission channel, fee and evidence type expected for each row
actions: For each row enter the channel (NAIC Financial Data Repository, state portal, filing email, hard copy), the copy count, the notarisation requirement and the fee amount and payment method.
Enter the evidence type that will close the row: NAIC confirmation reference, portal receipt, email delivery receipt or courier proof of delivery.
Name the internal owner for the row and their backup so no row depends on one person's availability.
Flag rows whose channel changed from last year so the owner reads the new instruction before filing.
checklist.done: every row carries a channel, fee, evidence type, owner and backup, with channel changes flagged.

checklist.step: Arm the reminder schedule against every row
actions: Configure reminders per row at T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-2 business days before the due date, addressed to the named owner and copied to the backup.
Configure the T-2 escalation alert to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for any row still showing no confirmation.
Test-fire one reminder per filing type after configuration and confirm delivery to the named owner.
Record in the calendar the date the reminders were armed and by whom.
checklist.done: reminders and the T-2 escalation are armed on every row, test-fired for each filing type and dated in the calendar.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar quarterly against licence movements
actions: Each quarter, re-extract the licence register and compare it to the calendar's jurisdiction list per entity.
Open a calendar row for every new licence, dated from the certificate of authority effective date, before the next filing deadline.
Close rows for surrendered licences only once the state's written withdrawal acknowledgement and any final-statement requirement are on file.
Log each change with the evidence reference and the date, and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve it.
checklist.done: the quarterly refresh reconciles the calendar to the licence register with every add and close evidenced and approved.

checklist.step: Refresh due dates and channels against new state bulletins
actions: Monitor the domiciliary and major-state insurance department bulletin pages and the NAIC instruction updates monthly for financial-reporting changes.
For each change, identify every affected calendar row and update the due date, channel or fee, pasting the bulletin citation and effective date onto the row.
Notify the affected row owners of the change in writing and confirm they have read it.
Have the Controller approve any due-date change before it replaces the existing row value.
checklist.done: every bulletin affecting a filing date or channel is reflected on the affected rows with a citation and a Controller approval.

checklist.step: Capture the confirmation on each row as the filing is made
actions: As each filing is submitted, attach to the calendar row the evidence type the row demands — NAIC Financial Data Repository confirmation reference, portal receipt PDF, delivery receipt or courier proof of delivery.
Enter the actual filing date read from the confirmation, not from the submission attempt, and let the calendar compute days early or late.
Reject an internal 'sent' note as evidence where the row demands a regulator-side acknowledgement.
File the confirmation in the compliance evidence repository under entity / year / period and link it from the calendar row.
checklist.done: every filed row carries a regulator-side confirmation, a filing date read from that confirmation and a repository link.

checklist.step: Run the monthly unfiled-item reconciliation
actions: On the first business day of each month, list every calendar row with a due date in the prior month and no confirmation attached.
List every row due in the current month with no owner activity recorded, and chase the owner the same day.
Compare the calendar's filed rows to the statutory reporting software's filing history so a filing made but not logged is caught.
Publish the reconciliation output to the Controller with the open-row count and the named owners.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation publishes the open-row count with named owners and reconciles the calendar to the software filing history.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk rows before the due date passes
actions: Work the T-2 escalation alerts daily and contact each row owner for a same-day status and a completion time.
Where the owner cannot complete, reassign to the backup immediately rather than waiting for the due date.
Where the row will miss its date, raise a tracker issue before the deadline passes and notify the Controller and the Compliance Officer in writing the same day.
Record the escalation, the reassignment and the outcome on the calendar row.
checklist.done: every T-2 alert has a same-day owner response, a reassignment where needed, and any expected miss is escalated before the date passes.

checklist.step: Maintain the exception log for missed and late rows
actions: Open an issue for every row filed after its due date or closed without a confirmation, naming entity, jurisdiction, filing type, due date and actual date.
Assign a root cause — calendar row missing, wrong due date, wrong channel, owner unavailable, evidence not captured — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a missed statutory deadline, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Review open issues with the Regulatory Reporting Manager monthly until closed.
checklist.done: every late or unconfirmed row has an issue with a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a monthly review until closure.

checklist.step: Report the timeliness scorecard each quarter
actions: Produce the scorecard: rows due, rows filed on time, on-time percentage by jurisdiction and by filing type, late rows with days late, and open exceptions.
Trend the on-time percentage against the prior four quarters so a drift is visible before it becomes a miss.
Send the scorecard to the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer within 10 business days of each quarter's 45-day deadline.
Add the scorecard to the Audit Committee reporting pack.
checklist.done: a quarterly scorecard with on-time percentage, trend and open exceptions reaches the Controller and CFO within 10 business days.

checklist.step: Version and archive the calendar so timeliness can be proved after the fact
actions: Export the calendar at each quarter end as a dated, read-only version showing due dates, actual dates, confirmation references and owners.
File the export with the confirmation set under entity / year / quarter and apply the 7-year retention label from the filing date.
Keep the change history so any due-date change can be shown with its date, its source citation and its approver.
Confirm the archive is searchable by entity, jurisdiction, filing type and period.
checklist.done: a dated read-only calendar export with change history is archived under a 7-year label and searchable by jurisdiction and period.

checklist.step: Rehearse an examiner timeliness request against the archive
actions: Pick three jurisdictions and one prior year at random and produce the due date, actual filing date and confirmation reference for every filing type without asking the row owner for help.
Time the exercise against the 5-business-day examination-response commitment and record the elapsed time.
Fix any gap the rehearsal exposes — missing confirmation, unindexed export, unresolvable reference — before an examiner finds it.
File the rehearsal note with the result and the fixes applied.
checklist.done: the rehearsal produces a complete timeliness record for the selected jurisdictions inside 5 business days, with every gap fixed and noted.

checklist.step: Refresh owner assignments and access when people move
actions: Review calendar row ownership monthly against the current Finance and Regulatory Reporting org list from HR.
Reassign every row owned by a leaver or a mover within 5 business days and confirm the new owner's reminder delivery.
Confirm each owner and backup still holds the filing credentials their rows need — NAIC iSite+ access and the relevant state portal logins.
Record the reassignment date and the credential check on the row.
checklist.done: no calendar row is owned by a leaver, every reassignment is within 5 business days and each owner's filing credentials are confirmed.

checklist.step: Close the year and carry forward the calendar baseline
actions: Review the year's on-time percentage, late rows and root causes with the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Compliance Officer.
Convert each recurring root cause into a change to next year's calendar build — a missing filing type, a wrong channel, an owner concentration.
Approve the closing calendar version as the baseline for the January rebuild.
Report the year's timeliness result and the agreed changes to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: the year's root causes are converted into calendar build changes and the closing baseline is approved and reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: Rebuild the expected calendar row set independently
actions: Extract the licence register directly and expand every active certificate of authority into entity × jurisdiction rows without reference to the existing calendar.
Add the filing types from the current-year NAIC Annual and Quarterly Statement Instructions and each sampled state's own checklist.
Record the rebuilt row count, the entity list and the extract date in the workpaper.
Cross-check the entity list against the NAIC company listing so an unregistered entity cannot be omitted.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt row set exists with its count and source dates recorded and cross-checked to the NAIC company listing.

testing.step: Reconcile the live calendar to the rebuilt row set
actions: Join the rebuilt rows to the live calendar on entity + jurisdiction + filing type + period.
List every rebuilt row absent from the calendar as an automatic exception — a missing row is the failure mode that produces a missed filing.
List every calendar row absent from the rebuild and confirm it reflects a genuine obligation rather than a stale licence.
Compute calendar completeness as a percentage and compare it to the 100% threshold.
testing.done: calendar completeness is computed against the rebuilt row set and every missing or extra row is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of calendar rows
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary rows, all rows with an overridden due date, all rows whose channel changed in the year and all rows with a logged exception.
Draw 25 further rows at random across jurisdictions and filing types using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the coverage percentage in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample spans quarterly blank, annual blank, audited report and supplement filing types.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers domiciliary rows, overrides, channel changes, exceptions and every filing type.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled row's due date from the primary source
actions: For quarterly blank rows recompute quarter end + 45 days and compare to the calendar value (March 31 → May 15, June 30 → August 14, September 30 → November 14).
For annual rows compare to the fixed dates — March 1 Annual Blank and RBC, April 1 Insurance Expense Exhibit, June 1 audited report, August 1 internal control communication.
For overridden rows read the cited state checklist entry or bulletin yourself and confirm it says what the row claims.
Any difference between the recomputed and recorded due date is an exception, including a right date resting on a wrong citation.
testing.done: every sampled due date recomputes from the primary source and every override citation is independently verified.

testing.step: Verify the recorded channel and evidence type against the state checklist
actions: For each sampled row, open the state's entry in the current-year NAIC statement instructions filing checklist and read the required channel, copy count, notarisation and fee.
Compare each attribute to the calendar row and list every difference.
Confirm the row's required evidence type matches what that channel can actually produce — a hard-copy row demanding a portal receipt is a design fault.
Capture the checklist page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: channel, copy count, notarisation, fee and evidence type on each sampled row agree to the captured current-year checklist page.

testing.step: Test confirmation coverage across the whole calendar
actions: List every calendar row with a due date in the period under test and check each has an attached confirmation in the evidence repository.
Open each sampled confirmation and confirm it is regulator-side (NAIC reference, portal receipt, delivery receipt, courier proof) rather than an internal sent note.
Confirm the filing date on the row was read from the confirmation by comparing the two.
Compute confirmation coverage as a percentage of due rows.
testing.done: confirmation coverage is computed and every sampled confirmation is regulator-side with a matching filing date on the row.

testing.step: Re-perform the reminder and escalation configuration test
actions: For each sampled row, read the configured reminder set and confirm T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-2 reminders exist and address the named owner and backup.
Check the T-2 escalation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager is configured and confirm from the escalation log that it actually fired for at least one late row in the period.
Compare each row's owner to the current HR org list and flag any leaver still named.
Confirm each owner holds the NAIC iSite+ or state portal credentials their rows require.
testing.done: reminder and escalation configuration is verified on every sampled row, no leaver owns a row, and owner credentials are confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute the on-time percentage reported in the scorecard
actions: Recompute days late per row from the confirmation date and the recomputed due date, independent of the calendar's own calculation.
Recompute the on-time percentage by jurisdiction and by filing type and compare to the published scorecard.
Investigate any difference between your figure and the reported figure — a scorecard computed off filed rows rather than due rows overstates performance.
Confirm the scorecard reached the Controller and the CFO within 10 business days of the quarter's deadline.
testing.done: the recomputed on-time percentage agrees to the published scorecard, or the difference and its cause are stated.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, filing type, the calendar attribute at fault and the consequence.
Assign a root cause — row never created, licence movement not reflected, bulletin not picked up, wrong channel, evidence not captured, owner left — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require the calendar correction to be made and approved by the Controller before the issue closes.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a Controller-approved calendar correction before closure.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: State calendar completeness and confirmation coverage as percentages against the 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each missing row and each uncaptured confirmation.
Have the independent reviewer, who does not maintain the calendar and rebuilt the row set from the licence register and the NAIC checklists, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missing-row exposure to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states calendar completeness, confirmation coverage, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.
